subject: English
passage: The practice of controlled grazing (allowing livestock to feed on grasslands for limited periods) is often thought to be at odds with grassland conservation (the work of preserving natural grassland ecosystems). However, a comprehensive study in ecosystem management spanning 500,000 acres across Montana's Great Plains calls that view into question. So far, results of the study suggest that grassland areas that have undergone rotational grazing (the careful management of livestock movement across controlled sections) may be more biodiverse than areas that haven't been grazed at all. These results, in turn, suggest that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: controlled grazing may be useful for maintaining healthy grasslands, provided it is rotational.
choices.B: other ecosystem management strategies are more effective than rotational grazing.
choices.C: as time passes, it will be difficult to know whether rotational grazing has any benefits.
choices.D: the best way to support grassland health may be to leave large areas entirely ungrazed.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it most logically completes the text's discussion of the potential effects of controlled grazing on grassland conservation. The text begins by stating that grazing practices are often thought of as being contrary to grassland conservation efforts. Then, the text presents the results of a research study examining the effect of rotational grazing practices on specific grassland areas, finding that the areas with rotational grazing may be "more biodiverse" (healthier) than the areas that hadn't been grazed at all. Given these results, it follows that controlled grazing may be a useful practice for maintaining healthy grasslands if it is practiced in a rotational way.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect because the study referenced in the text only provides information on rotational grazing as a potential ecosystem management strategy. There is no information in the text about how other ecosystem management strategies support grassland conservation efforts. Therefore, the text does not support the assertion that other ecosystem management strategies are more successful than rotational grazing.
